add_paragraph: Michael founded CLEAR WATER LAB in 2016 after six years at ETH Zürich. His group studies how carbon moves through soil — from root-scale chemistry to catchment-scale fluxes — and builds the field instrumentation needed to measure it continuously.
He leads the lab's Alpine monitoring network and serves as principal investigator on two EU-funded projects on soil carbon sequestration.

His current focus is the ==rhizosphere==: the narrow zone around living roots where exudates, microbes and minerals meet — and where, as the lab's warming experiment suggests, **temperature variability matters more than mean warming**.
